messages:
customer-support: Heads-up — customer ricardo_acme on Private VPC (customer-managed kmr-gateway) reports intermittent 429s and p99 token latency spikes during short ingestion bursts. They see X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 in responses and occasional upstream-reset/502. Can infra/runtime take a look?

ricardo_acme: yes — we run a bulk import that spikes for ~30s, then drops. Happens ~every 15 minutes. We haven't changed traffic shape. No other errors in app logs.

maya_support: thanks ricardo — can you paste the gateway / ingress logs for one of the events? also which ingress: nginx/traefik/envoy?

ricardo_acme: kmr-gateway (customer proxy based on Envoy) + nginx-ingress in front of our pod. here's a snippet (sanitized):

```
[2026-02-08T14:12:03Z] "POST /v1/generate" 200 312ms - req_id=abc123
[2026-02-08T14:12:14Z] "POST /v1/generate" 429 6ms - X-RateLimit-Remaining:0 req_id=abc124
[2026-02-08T14:12:14Z] upstream reset: connection reset by peer
```

maya_support: ok — 429 suggests a rate limiter is firing somewhere (customer gateway or our edge). devin, any routing/rate policies that could trigger for Private VPC?

devin_runtime: not on Redwood side for that customer — Private control plane defers to customer-managed gateway for ingress. However, we do have fallback model variants and a short-term global concurrency cap on older Dedicated fallbacks, but that should return 503 or queue, not 429. Check customer gateway configs first.

jen_sre: couple of hypotheses: token-bucket/leaky-bucket mismatch between nginx and Envoy, or kube-proxy/ipvs mode causing short-term connection churn. Also HPA cooldowns can cause thundering herd after scale-down. Ask customer: what are kube ingress controller settings (burst, rate, limit_req_zone if nginx) and Envoy filter config?

ricardo_acme: nginx ingress is stock with limit_req in annotations: "limit_req: zone=api burst=20 nodelay" and Envoy has a local rate_limit filter with stage 0, descriptor for route /v1/generate limit=120r/m. We also have a sidecar that does TLS termination.

devin_runtime: two things stand out: (1) nginx burst=20 with nodelay allows short bursts, but Envoy's 120r/m = 2r/s will block after ~20 requests in ~10s — causing 429 once token bucket drains. (2) mismatch of time windows: nginx bursts might create microbursts hitting Envoy gate. Suggest aligning rate limits or raising Envoy descriptor to match expected burst throughput for import window.

maya_support: ricardo — can you try a quick repro by running a 30s burst at 200r/s from a test client and stream logs? If 429s appear from Envoy, modify the Envoy descriptor to something like 1000r/60s during the import window or use a higher burst setting on Envoy token bucket.

ops-bot: deploy note: altering Envoy rate limit descriptors requires restarting the kmr-gateway deployment or triggering a config reload. If you need a quick patch, switch the global limiter to a permissive policy for that route.

ricardo_acme: did a test run. Confirmed: initial ~25 requests pass then 429s from Envoy. Nginx never 429s. Changing Envoy limiter to 600r/m temporarily eliminated 429s during import.

jen_sre: good repro. Next steps: two options — (A) adjust Envoy descriptor to support scheduled imports (higher burst/window) and add predicate for source IP or route; or (B) implement a client-side backoff + concurrency limit to smooth bursts. Also examine kube-proxy mode: if scale-down happened, pods may receive connection spikes when new ones come up.

devin_runtime: I'd also recommend enabling prefix/KV caching on the Redwood side for repeated token patterns (if import is using similar prompts) — that reduces ingress load. For long-term, consider rate-limit coordination: set nginx to be a soft gate (lower strictness) and keep the authoritative limiter in a single place to avoid mismatched windows.

maya_support: ricardo — I'll draft a short runbook you can apply:
- Temporarily raise Envoy descriptor for /v1/generate to 600r/m during import windows
- Add route-level exception for known importer IPs (or add auth header whitelisting)
- If using nginx limit_req, set burst to match Envoy capacity or remove nginx limit for that route
- Put a short HPA scale-up window before scheduled import to avoid cold-start spikes

ricardo_acme: thanks — will test changes tomorrow in staging. one quick Q: is there any Redwood-side quota that could still issue 429s even after they fix gateway?

devin_runtime: only for hosted customers we enforce token quotas. For Private VPC the control plane shouldn't impose runtime 429s for customer traffic. If you see Redwood-sourced 429s, collect the response headers (x-rw-*) and escalate.

maya_support: tagging follow-up: once ricardo verifies staging, we'll add the config diffs to the support ticket and schedule a brief config review. :thumbsup:

ricardo_acme: test in staging succeeded with Envoy=600r/m and temporary nginx removal for that route. No more 429s in the 30s bursts. We'll put a permanent IP-based exception and longer HPA warmup. Thanks everyone.

jen_sre: nice. please capture the final configs and add notes about why the mismatch caused the 429s (helps future customers). closing pending doc update. :white_check_mark:
